summary: The note covers Belarus's first democratic presidential election, held after a new constitution was enacted in early 1994. It lists the six first-round candidates and their vote shares, and notes Lukashenko's 80.1% win in the July 10 second round. It also describes his post-election address to the State Duma in Moscow, where he proposed a Union of Slavic states that would lead to the Union of Russia and Belarus in 1999.
one_line: Covers Alexander Lukashenko's 1994 election as Belarus's first democratically elected president and his early proposal for a Slavic union with Russia.
key_facts: A new Belarusian constitution enacted in early 1994 paved the way for the first democratic presidential election on 23 June and 10 July.
Six candidates stood in the first round of the Belarusian presidential election, including Alexander Lukashenko.
Alexander Lukashenko campaigned as an independent on a populist platform.
Shushkevich and Kebich also ran in the presidential election, with Kebich regarded as the clear favorite.
Alexander Lukashenko won 45.1% of the vote in the first round.
Kebich received 17.4% of the vote in the first round.
Zyanon Paznyak received 12.9% of the vote in the first round.
Shushkevich, along with two other candidates, received less than 10% of the votes in the first round.
Alexander Lukashenko won the second round of the election on 10 July with 80.1% of the vote.
Shortly after his election, Alexander Lukashenko addressed the State Duma of the Russian Federation in Moscow.
Alexander Lukashenko proposed a new Union of Slavic states in his address to the State Duma.
The proposed Union of Slavic states would culminate in the creation of the Union of Russia and Belarus in 1999.
